iconicAnchor.label: Hector Guimard's Kantirix perfume bottle
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Perfume-vessel design and sensory product presentation
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: Cooper Hewitt presents Guimard's perfume bottle as a small abstract glass sculpture within a complete designed style, establishing the vessel as the campaign's sensory and material anchor.

sources.title: Hector Guimard: How Paris Got Its Curves
supports: Perfume bottles can function as small sculptural objects whose glass, silhouette, and finish carry a designed identity.
The vessel belongs within a broader material and marketing system rather than operating as an arbitrary luxury prop.

sources.title: Scent Bottle, 1800-1860
supports: Pattern-molded blown glass provides concrete evidence for small scale, surface relief, transparency, and vessel construction.
The object record supports physically plausible glass detail while the campaign guidance adds atmosphere and narrative.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches sensual, glass, lacquer, object scale, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/scent-campaign/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
